$comment: KG (Source) disposition manifest for every PACT v2.3 vector id OUTSIDE spec/v2.3/conformance/extended/execution-boundary (#5567). Hand-authored, machine-verified — the execution-boundary-acceptance.json pattern: conformance-dispositions.test.ts pins (a) that these 36 ids plus execution-boundary-acceptance.json's 2 executed + 9 capability-excluded ids are EXACTLY the 47-id expected_vector_ids the generated fixture carries from pact's own manifest — disjoint, no phantoms, no id claimed twice; (b) that every capability flag a family cites is live-FALSE on the served profile (buildPactProfile(), the same builder /.well-known/pact.json serializes) and every cited declared gap is live on the wire, so the day a flag flips to true the suite goes red and the family must be re-dispositioned rather than kept as a stale exclusion; (c) that every entry carries a reason, every skip carries a tracking reference, and every skip's `requires` flags are live-TRUE (a skip claims the vector is executable in principle). The results document (src/lib/pact-conformance-report.ts) publishes these verbatim under the pact runner vocabulary: excluded = not executable against this implementation BY ITS OWN SERVED DECLARATION; skip = executable in principle, not yet harnessed, tracked. Neither is ever a silently dropped vector.
scope: every expected_vector_ids entry not under extended/execution-boundary/ — that family (11 ids) is dispositioned by execution-boundary-acceptance.json

families.reason: kind: verification — the §17.7 authorization-proof verification flow (envelope and structural checks, freshness, nonce binding, principal resolution, credential revocation, and for real-signature vectors the cryptographic check). The KG verifies no authorization_proof of any kind: capabilities.authorizationProof is served false (AUTHORIZATION_PROOF_SUPPORTED in effect-class.ts) and the '§17.4 / §17.6 principals and proofs' declared gap states there is no HumanPrincipal registry and no proof verification. There is no seam a proof could enter, so no attestation vector — positive or negative — is executable against this implementation. Tailor's separate C# guard executes this family (tests/WebApi.UnitTests/Fixtures/PactV23, #5640); that is a different implementation and is not claimable for the KG.

kind: mandate — drives the §19–§20 Mandate guard (pact's mcp/ reference implementation of au.tailor.pact/mandate) locally with an injected clock, registry mutation, mid-session revocation and escalation retry. The KG has no mandate guard, no mandate registry and no MCP tool surface such a guard would wrap: capabilities.mandates is served false. Nothing here consumes a mandate, so no mandate vector is executable against this implementation.

kind: http — the Matter surface (open a matter, attach a fabric, post a matter message, the cross-fabric matter manifest, close without cascade). The KG serves no matter route — the API table in PACT_CONFORMANCE.md is the complete /api/pact route tree, drift-gated, and carries none — and capabilities.matters is served false. Each vector's preconditions fix a matter server_state that is unconstructible against this implementation, by declaration rather than by omission.

kind: http / session — the session surface: atomic onboard (onboard-success, onboard-partial-failure rest on capabilities.atomicOnboard), the session manifest with cross-org disclosure (manifest-cross-org-disclosure rests on capabilities.manifest), and session awareness — heartbeat timeout, obligation surfacing and the two-agent negotiation smoke (rest on capabilities.sessionAwareness). All three flags are served false; the KG has no onboard, manifest or heartbeat route. The topic read that stands in for /_status and /manifest inside the two EXECUTED execution-boundary vectors is a declared surface mapping over an existing route, not a manifest capability — which is exactly why capabilities.manifest stays false and why none of these six is executable.

vectors.reason: Executable in principle: the KG serves POST /api/pact/{topicId}/join-token and advertises capabilities.inviteTokens true — precisely the anonymous invite-token join this vector drives. No adapter exists yet in execution-boundary-vectors.itest.ts (seeding the invite token from the vector's server_state, dispatching its request to the real route module, and pinning the value-level divergences the KG's join-token wire carries: contextMode 'full' where the vector expects 'scoped', and the KG's own pact.agent.joined payload shape). Until it runs, the honest verdict is skip, not excluded; the adapter is tracked.
